copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Norway v Senegal in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Tuesday, and the model and the market disagree on the Senegal side by +13.0pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

Public Elo rates Senegal 30 points higher than the other side (Norway 1760, Senegal 1790). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Norway to win at 33%, the draw at 28%, and Senegal to win at 39%. The away side reads 39% on this distribution — the model's central case for Senegal.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Norway to win at 48%, the draw at 25%, and Senegal to win at 26%. Polymarket has Senegal at 26%, which prices out at American odds of +285; the model has the same side at 39%. The +13.0pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Senegal side that lower bound is 32% — +5.8pp clear of the market's 26%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding Senegal priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 31 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-match Elo gives Senegal a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +13.0pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
This is a selection call on the Senegal side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +13.0pp gap across model and market on the Senegal side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Senegal at 39%; Polymarket sits at 26%.
copy.title: Norway v Senegal · the model leans Senegal
